findings: Historical resolver success binds package/user/component and prior no-launch state but does not authorize launch: launch worker resolves again and requires exact COMPONENT before original launch_locked.
Launch and inspection hold one external global action lock; cleanup holds only the flow lock and delegates global lock ownership to original Flow.cleanup, avoiding a nested acquisition.
Original native launch requires no preexisting target task, one durable launch-attempt marker, exact native host receipt, exact new leaf and task-set delta before launch-scope is written.

Native launch command admits only exact argv/component, one claim, timeout70 and mutation=true; inspect only fixed before/state, inspect, after/state nonces. No click, text, media or screenshot authority is added.

Count gates align with callsites: launch 4 target + 4 helper metadata + one resolver + two stacks + one native launch =12 durable commands; inspect 4 target +8 helper +2 stacks +3 instrumentation =17, with 3 private foreground reads separately admitted.

Coordinator requires successful durable launch before starting inspect. A failed phase stops the business sequence; independently authorized original exact-task cleanup still runs only if valid fresh launch-scope exists. Uncertain launch without scope is retained for reconciliation, not broadened into a package stop.

Cleanup requires original exact leaf removal or confirmed already-absent task and equality with the prelaunch task set. Durable success additionally requires held binding/three APK FD release, unchanged helper/target/Main, source stability and no secondary errors.

The original remember helper preserves first error, appends secondary cleanup/guard/write errors and forces ok=false. The shared source loaded by qualified() and pure receipt summary does not initiate another Android action.
